status: ENGINE CORE built 2026-10-08 (tools/dungeon.py, pack cobblers_dungeons): the timer, the greed ladder's counter, the slots and their shells, the staged boss's chain, the recall sweep, E1's engine half, entry and exit, the sigils and the rip. Generated and unit-tested; NOTHING of it has run on a server (experiments/EXP-084-dungeon-engine-core, NOT_EXECUTED). NOT built (step 6): the stands and their clawback, the seam markers and rate source, the parkour catch bands, the lake and the den. The Night Shift is full length on the room kit since DG-NS (2026-10-09: its rooms, its clock_s_by_band); the kinds the wave-2 builders implement (stand, gauntlet, miniboss, nest, habitat, puzzle, vault, the healer) build as themed empty rooms until they merge.
rung: datapack plus functions/commands (CLAUDE.md principle 6): vanilla scoreboards, bossbars, interactions, advancements and recipes, and Cobblemon 1.8.0's own commands (spawnnpcat, runmolang) and battle_victory callback. Every lower rung is exhausted by the record DUNGEONS.md 11.1 cites (DM 4.1: no 1.8.0 callback can cancel anything, so no-deploy is a sweep; DM 1.1: no native run timer). Nothing here is a mod, a script layer or a companion.
tunable: EVERY clock, delay and threshold below is tunable data, not a decided number: probe XT1 (EXP-079) timed no fight, so the band clocks are DUNGEONS.md 4.2's planning values (relayed), and the delays are the engine's own choices

engine.pack_why: world-local (tools/reapply.py WORLD_LOCAL): the keeper kills players on a timer, spawns NPCs, takes and gives items and sets game modes on its own; the global datapacks folder is loaded by every world the server runs, the live one included

pocket.read_from: data/portals.json pocket.dimension and pocket.floor_y, and data/entei_boss.json pocket.border and border_margin: tools/dungeon.py fails closed if any disagrees (as tools/entei_boss.py does). The dimension is cobblers_portals' and registers only at a boot

slots.why: DUNGEONS.md section 1: 4 slots per dungeon, one strip each, 2,048 long in x and at most 64 wide in z, 128-block rows from z 1,024. Slot k of dungeon d is row (d-1)*4 + (k-1): its strip is z0 = rows_from_z + row * row_spacing .. z0 + strip_width_max - 1, x origin_x .. origin_x + strip_length - 1, its spine along +x at the strip's centre line z0 + strip_width_max / 2. tools/dungeon.py refuses any overlap with the portals' rescue box (z -512..768 on every x), Entei's band (z around -768) and the probe pack's row (z -704..-577, data/dungeon_probes.json), each recomputed from its own file
slots.overworld_coincidence: the rows are inside the overworld map's x/z bounds (data/world.json 0..8191), unlike Entei's (data/entei_boss.json pocket.origin_why). What that risks is the blackout's waystone arrival test, which compares coordinates and not dimensions (data/blackout.json checkpoints.waystone_jump_why): tools/dungeon.py refuses any slot's arrival point within waystone_arrival_radius + 1 of a town waystone in data/progression.json, and the keeper's own box tests are made dimension-safe by the dg.pk tag (a box test on @s is coordinate-only)
slots.clear_strip_why: false for the placeholder: the pocket is void, so the shell writes only its own boxes. A shell from an earlier, LONGER spine is not cleared by a later shorter one; set true for the first apply of the real spine (step 4) to air the whole strip first (I2, EXP-081: one 2,048 x 64 strip cleared in one function call stalls the server 2.64 s fresh). A re-apply step only, never at entry

engine.members_why: solo first (D16). The data and the scores carry a member index (bossbar ..._m1) so co-op is a switch, not a rewrite; the gates, the bar and the slot's freeing are written per member

keeper.arrive_delay_why: Entei's (data/entei_boss.json keeper.arrive_delay_ticks), counted by the keeper on the player, so a player who logs out before arriving arrives when they return: at least 40 ticks after door_click, at most 40 + one period
keeper.entry_hold_why: an engine choice, not in DUNGEONS.md: a member who has paid but not crossed the threshold holds no clock, so 2.6's slot deadline would never come. This many ticks of absence before the threshold frees the slot; on their return the run is void and the sigil returned (the threshold refund, 7.4). Five minutes
keeper.rip_particle_why: DUNGEONS.md 7.1: re-emitted every 10 ticks while a player is within 48 blocks, so an unvisited rip costs one distance check. V1 (EXP-080) found these particles cannot be seen from 64-128 blocks; the plume is gated on the owner's look (rips[].plume)
keeper.boss_restart_why: an engine choice: a forfeit or flee sends no battle result (DM 1.4), which would leave a stage standing with the exit gate shut. After this many passes out of battle with the stage standing and no result, the keeper starts the same stage's battle again

clock.ladder_basis: D13 (the owner, 2026-10-08): x1.25 at 5, x1.5 at 10, x2.0 at 15, x3 at 20, per member, holding for the rest of the run. Quarter-ticks, so x1.25 is an integer rate (DUNGEONS.md 2.1)
clock.why: DUNGEONS.md 2.1-2.2: dg.clock on the player in quarter-ticks, the keeper subtracting period_ticks x rate each pass; no rate 0 (D1); titles at 5:00 and 1:00 and each of the last 10 seconds

return_margin.why: DUNGEONS.md 2.3: back_s = (x - x_back) x 10 / 56 (sprint 5.6 blocks a second, relayed GYM_INTERIORS.md:139), plus the parkour's re-crossing once past it (0: the placeholder spine has no parkour); the warning fires when real seconds left at the current rate fall under back_s + 60

engine.lockout_why: D17: one hour of UPTIME per dungeon per player, counted from the threshold (2.5). Our own counter (#up dg.up, 20 a keeper pass), never gametime, so a re-export or /time set cannot move it. It must be at least the longest clock (39 minutes = 46,800 ticks)
engine.bands_why: DUNGEONS.md 5.3 (caps) and 4.2's planning table (relayed: 29, 31, 32, 34, 37, 39 minutes). A player's band is the first whose highest cap is at or above their RCT level cap at the rip (5.1), frozen for the run. The clocks are for the REAL spine's walk and fights; with the placeholder spine V3 (clock = ceil(required x slack) over the built shell) cannot hold and is not claimed

death.rule:
E1 (DUNGEONS.md 11.3), the engine half: door_click adds the run tag in the function that reserves the slot, BEFORE the arrival delay, and cancels any tail still counting; the engine never removes the tag; after every way out (a clean exit, the eject, the respawn after a death, the dead-run kill, a run voided before the threshold) it starts a tail of tail_ticks + period_ticks on its own score dg.tail and, when it ends with the player OUTSIDE cobblers:pocket, runs `execute as

at @s run function `; its overworld sweep runs for a tagged player outside the pocket with no live run and no tail. Neither is ever called in the pocket. Every NPC the engine spawns carries claims.exempt_tag in the function that spawns it, and the keeper re-asserts it on any untagged NPC in a slot a pass later
death.tail_why: tail_ticks + period_ticks: the tail is counted down period_ticks per keeper pass, and a tail started between passes (a click) would otherwise end up to period_ticks - 1 short of tail_ticks
death.pre_threshold_death_why: an engine choice: a death before the threshold (nothing in the entry room can kill, so /kill or a wild hit at the rip's mouth while arriving) does not return the sigil; only a walk out by the back rip does (7.4)
death.titles_why: DUNGEONS.md 2.5, by cause (dg.cause): 1 the timer, 2 a boss stage (or any NPC) beat them, 3 anything else, 4 a run that died while they were away (2.6)
chat: Your items are all still yours. Nothing in a rift keeps them.
The blackout's money is gone for good. No one in the rift is holding it.
Kept: everything you mined and picked up.
death.chat_why: DUNGEONS.md 2.5's lines 1, 2 and 4, as drafted there (trainer-balance-designer to tone). Line 2 is printed without the amount (the blackout's own line names it); line 3 (the escrow) and line 5 (the lockout) are built by the keeper from scores
death.away_line: The rift closed while you were away.
death.away_line_why: 2.6's line, without its minutes: the slot's deadline is freed with the slot, so the minutes are not kept

escrow.status: the extension point only: no reward table is built tonight (section 9 is step 6's). A clean exit runs dungeons/pay, which is empty but for clearing dg.esc; every other way out clears it. dg.bossd is set when the boss's last stage falls, the flag 9.1's boss escrow will key on

clawback.status: BUILT 2026-10-09 (tools/dungeon_fights.py, unit DG-CLAW), NOT RUN IN GAME: every dungeon NPC battle (the boss's stages now, the stands through claw/begin and claw/bounds/<class>) takes CobbleDollars' own NPC-win payout back, by the arena's design (tools/arena_runtime.py cd/*; EXP-060, NOT_EXECUTED, is the arena's proof of the same timing assumption). claw/begin reads the balance before start_battle, a tick function re-reads it every tick until the result, the victory callback runs claw/settle, which takes the gain (at most dg.cmax, the most CobbleDollars can credit for that class) now or, if CobbleDollars' handler has not run yet, at the start of the next tick (dg.claw 1 while pending; sudden death's kill waits, E1 rule 6). The dungeon pays no purse of its own, so the whole payout goes back: $0 net
clawback.assumptions: the handler order and the inter-tick timing (EXP-060 for the arena); the exact level sum of an NPC's party (simple party, explicit level=); CobbleDollars crediting a win won inside cobblers:pocket like any other
clawback.does_not_cover: a player offline in the tick after the win keeps dg.claw 1 until they return (the tick function then takes it); a battle with no result (flee, forfeit) pays nothing and so takes nothing

stands.status: the generator of the trainer classes and the stand battle's start, built by tools/dungeon_fights.py; the room kinds stand and gauntlet/ambush (unit DG-FIGHTS, 2026-10-09) seat them and dispatch each win to the room's clear; no authored dungeon carries one yet, the fixture tests/fixtures/dungeon_fights_rooms.json does
stands.level_rule: DUNGEONS.md 5.3: members 2/3/3/4/5/6 by band, levels from the band's lower cap less low_offset to the lower cap less high_offset, the last (the ace) at the high end; band 6 spans band6_levels. Never above the band's lower cap
stands.go_ticks_why: the battle starts go_ticks after the macro spawn: Heaven's Arena's GO_TICKS (tools/arena_runtime.py), proven in game 2026-10-03 for its macro-free spawn; L1/C1 only needed a tick

adventure.rule: the arrival sets adventure and the tag; every way out, and the overworld backstop for a tagged player with no live run outside the pocket, sets survival and removes it. Only a player WE put in adventure is ever set to survival (V13)

sweep.rule: DUNGEONS.md 3.4: every keeper pass, in each no-deploy box of a slot whose run is live, every cobblemon:pokemon without dg.keep is removed by `execute as <it> run runmolang "q.entity.discard;"` (P1's form 2, EXP-069 step 5: PASS on a wild Pokemon), every player in the box is dismounted, and ender pearls are killed. Never `kill`
sweep.gated_on: P1 (owner half): discarding an OWNED sent-out Pokemon, and that it returns to the party with its HP kept (DM 4.2), is unproven
sweep.message: The rift will not hold them here.

sigils.accept_rule: one of the entrant's own band if held, else the lowest higher band held; only a lower band's: refused, 'This sigil is too weak for you now.' (7.4)
sigils.custom_data_type_why: FINDING (2026-10-08): SG1 (EXP-083) step 5 proved `[custom_data~{cobblers_dg_sigil:1}]` against a sherd STOCKED with an int 1, but step 7 read the CRAFTED sigil as `cobblers_dg_sigil: 1b` (a recipe's JSON number becomes the smallest NBT type). An NBT partial match compares tag types (1b is not 1), so the int predicate would very likely never match a crafted sigil. The engine matches, gives and refunds the byte form throughout; the match against a CRAFTED sigil is unproven (EXP-084 step SG)

That only overpays (the rip checks the band)

rip_art.why: the owner (2026-10-09): the dungeon rip should look like the Cobblemon Ultra Beasts mod's wormhole: an upright oval, a soft puffy pink cloud ring round a lavender band round a pale blue glowing centre. That mod is not installed and its art was never fetched or copied; tools/rip_art.py draws our own, from the description alone. tools/rip_pack.py packs it as a CLIENT resource pack (never installed on the server); tools/dungeon.py R16DR shows it with an item_display
rip_art.item_why: the carrier: a vanilla item whose model our pack overrides ONLY for this custom_model_data (1.21.1 item overrides, assets/minecraft/models/item/<item>.json 'overrides' with a 'custom_model_data' predicate; the component is a plain int in 1.21.1). A player without the pack sees a large flat amethyst shard where the rip stands, which still reads as a rift and is never a white square
rip_art.frame_why: 3:4, the oval's own proportion, so the 3 x 4 block quad shows it undistorted
rip_art.loop_why: 48 frames x 5 ticks = 240 ticks = 12 s a loop: the outer clouds turn once a loop (slow), the core beats twice (every 6 s). Interpolated, so the five ticks between frames blend
rip_art.brightness_why: a display entity's own `brightness` override (the 1.21.1 display-entity NBT): full light, so the oval glows at night and in a cave mouth instead of taking the light of the block it stands in. A resource pack cannot make an item model emissive; this is the vanilla way

dungeons.rooms_why: DG-NS (2026-10-09), after the owner played the placeholder ('That was it?'; 'make it wider'; 'full length dungeons'): the record moved from spine.segments to the room kit (docs/mechanics/DUNGEON_ROOMS.md). DUNGEONS.md 11.1's named beats are kept where they fit: the Lamp Room, the Main Drift, the Hand's stand, the Old Incline, the Powerhouse den (D11, now on the spine as a nest that does not gate), the Lower Face (the seam), the Wet Drift down to the Sump (the lake idea as a flooded habitat, Volcanion: DUNGEONS.md 8, approved D18), the Collapse (parkour, 4 sections), the Haulage (rails taken up: the Shotfirer and the Timberman step out of it), the gantry (now the collapsing bridge), the Shift Road rising to the Stope, the Shift Bell. The 300-block 5-wide drifts are gone: no connector is over 40 long or under 7 wide. Pacing: no two gating fights without a breather between (stand, puzzle, den, dark, mini-boss, seam, vault, sump, safe room, parkour, gauntlet, bridge, boss); the seam and the vault come before the hardest stretch (the sump, the Collapse, the Haulage, the Stope), so greed is a choice made with that ahead; the safe room two thirds in, after the Sump: from there the Collapse, the Haulage, the gantry and the Stope run with no heal. Trainer teams and the mini-boss and nest species are the mine's families (11 theme: Timburr, Machop, Geodude, Roggenrola, Onix, Diglett, Drilbur) and are PLACEHOLDERS for trainer-balance-designer, like the boss's crews

dungeons.shape_mix_why: pass 2 (the owner: 'really emphasize making rooms different shapes, not all boxes'): a room without its own `shape` takes the jungle theme's mix; most rooms here name theirs. The box-only kinds (maze, parkour, collapse bridge, set piece) and the stairs, vault and puzzle stay boxes
dungeons.clock_why: tools/dungeon_clock.py jungle (DUNGEON_ROOMS.md 7), re-derived by DG2-JUNGLE on 2026-10-10 over the four variants and, at the gorge, the slower way: required 32.4/36.4/36.9/40.9/43.4/46.4 min for bands 1-6; the clock is ceil((required + 20 s) x 1.25) to the minute (the tool alone gives 41/46/47/52/55/58). The 20 s is this unit's allowance for the lights-out set piece, which the tool walks as a plain room: its hall at the dark-room pace (about 60 blocks x 0.5 / 4 = 8 s) and its cue, rounded up. From the slack, by design: Zarude (an open habitat, about 6 min), the treasury, greed past the free tier. Every band is at most 60 min, so D17's hour applies (no lockout of its own). Planning paces, not measured (XT1 timed no fight)
dungeons.design: Pass 2 (unit DG2-JUNGLE, 2026-10-10), after the owner's walk of pass 1: fewer, richer rooms that turn, climb, drop and double back. The OUTER JUNGLE on the floor of the strip: the strangler thicket (maze), the troop's clearing (nest), then north and up the root stair into the canopy crossing (parkour), the poachers' camp (stand; a cracked secret in its bank). The GORGE is the fork: the rope bridge straight over (fast, a collapse that costs a fall) or down into the gorge, along the streambed and up the far bank (safe, longer). The wild orchard (resources, the greed choice; the treasury a side room off it). The TEMPLE: the colonnade of masks (ambush), the temple steps, then the route turns and walks back WEST along the cloister (whose wall the colonnade shares: the shortcut back toward the entry), down the well stair, and east again UNDER the colonnade through the undercroft (dark) to the old shrine (safe room, healer). Then the hard stretch on one heal: the sanctum (habitat, Zarude, open; a balcony secret), the glyph door (puzzle), the Tangle (mini-boss), the canopy closing over the hall (the set piece) and the altar (the Gardener). Fights never meet: a non-fight room stands between any two

rooms.name: The strangler thicket
rooms.why: hedges of jungle, mangrove and azalea leaves on a spanning tree with loops, so a wrong turn is not always a dead end; it leaves toward the south of the strip

rooms.name: The troop's clearing
rooms.why: a monkey troop living on the jungle floor, a ragged cavern of moss banks; the way on is a ledge two up in the north wall at the far end, open when the troop is gone

rooms.name: The root stair
rooms.why: the route turns north out of the clearing and climbs: in by the south wall, out four up a landing into the canopy

rooms.name: The canopy crossing
rooms.why: jungle-wood platforms on log pillars over a moss floor, winding across the strip with a hard and a safe line (PARKOUR2)

rooms.name: The poachers' camp

params.lore: A poacher's brass tag, notched forty times. Scratched under it: whatever we net, the Gardener's vines take back by morning.

rooms.why: the player fight: two poachers who net the jungle's Pokemon; their cache is walled up behind cracked temple stone in the north bank (the rift pick opens it)

rooms.name: The rope bridge
rooms.why: FAST AND DANGEROUS: straight over the gorge on a bamboo bridge that falls away behind the walker; a fall costs the clock and the bridge again

rooms.name: The streambed
rooms.why: SAFE AND LONG: six down, along the winding floor of the gorge, and up the far bank; nothing to fall from, more to walk
the FORK (DUNGEON_ROOMS.md 1a): two ways over the gorge out of the camp's east wall, rejoining at the orchard's west wall

rooms.name: The wild orchard
rooms.why: logs, melons, bamboo, honeycomb and pumpkins to take, each a step up the greed ladder: the last free choice before the temple

rooms.name: The treasury
rooms.why: the SIDE room: a dead end off the orchard's south wall, loot for time, never on the way
rooms.loot_why: PLACEHOLDER, trainer-balance-designer's to price: one stack per chest, ids checked in the Cobblemon 1.8.0 jar's lang file. Optional (gate open): each chest costs clock_cost_s, the greed

rooms.why: an optional SIDE room (DUNGEON_ROOMS.md 1a): the clock does not count it

rooms.name: The colonnade of masks
rooms.why: the temple's outer guard: two masked wardens step out between the columns and each holds its line until beaten

rooms.name: The temple steps
rooms.why: the temple's porch: the way on is through its north wall, and the route turns back west

rooms.name: The cloister
rooms.why: walked WEST beside the colonnade, sharing its wall: the SHORTCUT, a door from here back into the colonnade (toward the entry), opened from this side only

rooms.name: The well stair
rooms.why: still west, twelve down below the temple floor

rooms.name: The root well
rooms.why: the turn at the bottom: out by its south wall, under the colonnade

rooms.name: The undercroft
rooms.why: east again UNDER the colonnade and the steps (stacked rooms), roots through the vault and no light but the candles someone left

rooms.name: The old shrine
rooms.why: out of the dark into the shrine: the keeper heals the party, the one rest; after it the hard stretch on one heal (Zarude, the glyph door, the Tangle, the Gardener)

rooms.name: The sanctum

params.lore: A seed carved from green stone, warm to hold. The temple was raised to keep it, and Zarude was left to keep the temple.

rooms.why: the canopy hall, split in two levels, and the temple's keeper Zarude, the mythical of the deep jungle: OPEN, a fight the player may take or pass (the clock's slack pays for it). From the terrace a balcony looks over a gap to an alcove only it sees

rooms.name: The glyph door
rooms.why: five levers set to the glyph over the door; a wrong attempt costs the clock

rooms.name: The Tangle
rooms.why: a vine mass grown huge on the temple's water: Tangela, then Tangrowth from band 3. Fight only (D8)

rooms.name: Where the canopy closes
rooms.why: the SET PIECE before the boss: the canopy closes over the hall behind the walker, light by light

dungeons.variants_why: one per slot (slot k builds variants[k-1]; entry prefers one the player did not run last): a as authored; b mirrored north for south (doors, turns, the fork's sides, the secrets' walls); c re-rolled (every room's shape noise, dressing and the maze) with the glyph door a five-press sequence instead of the levers; d mirrored and re-rolled, the poachers lying in wait (the camp an ambush) and the Tangle's room a cavern. Every variant and both ways over the gorge pass the walk check (problems())

boss.name: The Temple Gardener

boss.teams_why: per band, one crew per stage, the ACE LAST: Thwackey to band 2 (Grookey's line evolves at 35), Rillaboom from band 3, the temple's drummer. boss.gated_on: C1 (owner half, EXP-078), as the Night Foreman's

rooms.why: the old sluice house: the rift lets out onto its dry floor, the board on the north wall; the door east is the threshold
worn steps down to where the water stands
MAZE: the reliquary's archive, its stacks fallen into a labyrinth of cracked, mossy walls
a flooded passage out of the stacks
STAND: the salvagers' camp in the first dry hall, two of the crew stripping the ruin, fought one after another (fossils they dredged up, and what a diver brings down)
a breather after the camp: a long wet gallery
PUZZLE: the sluice works, four levers to set to the pattern carved over the gate before the water lets you through
PARKOUR: the broken aqueduct, its arches fallen into the flooded undercroft; ledges and the stubs of piers to jump
a breather after the jumps
NEST: the cistern pool, a colony living in the drowned hall; the door opens when the colony is dealt with
a breather after the nest: an arcade half fallen in
DARK ROOM: the crypt under the reliquary, the water has put the lamps out; candles left by the salvagers, and three torches
AMBUSH: the salvage line, the crew's way out of the crypt; each steps out of the dark arcades as you cross their line, and you pass only by beating them
a breather after the ambush, the way the salvagers haul their finds
VAULT (greed): the offering hall, four chests the salvagers have not reached; each costs time on the clock. Optional: the door is open
a breather after the greed
MINI-BOSS: the guardian of the inner halls, a clay automaton the builders left to keep the way; it wakes when you cross the line
steps up out of the water to the dry upper halls
RESOURCES: where the reliquary's wall fell, ore shows in the broken face; every block taken speeds the clock (the greed ladder), before the hardest stretch
SAFE ROOM: a dry chapel two thirds in, where an old keeper of the ruin tends whoever reaches it
HABITAT (the set piece): the sealed chamber at the heart of the reliquary, flooded and tall, where the dragon the builders sealed away is still kept; seen from the door before it moves
COLLAPSING BRIDGE: the causeway over the drowned undercroft, falling away behind you
PUZZLE: the bell glyphs, struck in the order the lamps show to open the flood gate
the last passage, down to the flood chamber
the boss: the salvage master in the flood chamber, three crews dredged out of the ruin
the outflow: the far rip on its east wall

Sizes as the Foreman's (3/4/5 at band 1 to 6/6/6 at band 6). No species in her crews is a legendary
